metadata.title: Becoming Citizens in a Changing World
metadata.venue: IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study 2016 International Report

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This ICCS 2016 international report is based on a large-scale, multi-country assessment of lower secondary students, teachers, and schools. The study uses IEA’s standard complex survey sampling and scaling procedures to produce comparable estimates across countries; however, the provided excerpt does not specify the exact student weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife). For analyses using the ICCS 2016 international database, analysts should apply the IEA-provided sampling weights and replicate weights (if available) to account for stratification and clustering in the sample design. Because the excerpt does not report the specific weight variables or replicate scheme, weight usage cannot be confirmed from the text shown, but it is expected for population-representative inference in IEA studies.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The excerpt provided is a book/report front matter and foreword describing the ICCS 2016 study scope and sample, but it does not describe any student-level predictive modeling, plausible values (PV) generation, or PV-based outcome construction. ICCS includes scaled measures of civic knowledge and contextual variables, but the excerpt does not specify whether the report’s results rely on PVs, WLE/theta, or other scaling outputs. Therefore, PV handling and missing-data handling are not documented in the provided text, representing a reporting gap for this extraction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the full available ICCS 2016 study sample for the participating countries (24 countries), as described in the excerpt; the provided text does not specify any additional analytic subsample restrictions (e.g., grade-only, module-only, or complete-case filtering).

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2016 is the second cycle of the IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study and assesses lower secondary students’ civic knowledge and understanding, along with attitudes, perceptions, and engagement related to civic institutions and practices. The report describes that ICCS 2016 was conducted in 24 countries and includes measures designed to support comparisons with ICCS 2009, while also adding new focus areas such as social media use for civic engagement and concerns about global threats and sustainable development. The study draws on a comprehensive core assessment complemented by regional student questionnaires for Europe and Latin America. The excerpt indicates a large overall participation footprint (about 94,000 students, 37,000 teachers, and roughly 3,800 schools), but it does not provide the technical details needed here on scaling (PV vs. WLE/theta), missing-data procedures, or the specific statistical benchmarks used in the results chapters.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is extracted from the report’s front matter/foreword rather than from the methodological and results sections that would specify PV handling, missing-data treatment, analytic sample construction, and any ML modeling. As a result, the extraction cannot populate country-level sample sizes or any ML-related fields, and it cannot identify PV or missing-data procedures from the provided text. The study is an IEA large-scale assessment report (not an ML predictive paper), so main_findings and confounders_identified are intentionally left empty for this extraction scope.
